additional_info.body:
Dear Mr.Furkan,
As you mentioned that the fuse has tripped, we will need to plan a site intervention to inspect the fuses.
Kindly ensure that replacement fuses are carried along during the visit in case a replacement is required.
Steps to Check Fuses:
Isolate Power Supply:
Open the incoming circuit breaker (+F01-QA2) to disconnect the power supply
Confirm the circuit is de-energized using a multimeter
Visually Inspect the Fuse:
Look for signs of a blown fuse (discoloration, physical damage, melted elements, etc.).
Many MV fuses have inspection windows or indicators to show if the fuse has operated.
Remove the Fuse Safely:
Use insulated tools and follow proper procedures to remove the fuse.
Test the Fuse:
Use a
multimeter
check continuity
No continuity = blown fuse; continuity = fuse likely still good.
Inspect Fuse Holders and Contacts:
Check for carbonization, pitting, or looseness that may cause overheating or arcing.
Clean or replace damaged components as needed.
Replace the Fuse (if needed):
Use the exact same type and rating of fuse as specified.
Make sure it's properly seated and secured.
Re-energize the System:
Close the circuit breaker or switchgear after confirming all checks are complete.
Monitor operation and check for recurring issues.
